module.title: Unit 6: Best Friends: Friendship, Have to & Don't Have to
module.objective: Discuss friendship, social bonds, and personal duties using 'have to' and 'don't have to' to describe obligations.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Best Friends and Friendship Memories
subModules.grammarFocus: Past Simple (Irregular Verbs, Questions, Negatives) & Double Genitive

content.summary: Welcome to the reading module for Unit 6. In this lesson, you will read about best friends, personal qualities, and past experiences. You will learn how to use the Past Simple tense with irregular verbs, ask past questions, and use the double genitive structure.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Past Simple affirmative, negative, and questions with regular and irregular verbs, plus double genitive structures like a friend of mine.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Descriptive personality adjectives such as cheerful, generous, intelligent, and jealous, alongside emotional states.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts to find specific past time expressions and identifying main ideas about friendship and personal experiences.

learningObjectives: Understand short reading passages about past friendships and personal experiences.
Locate specific details regarding past events using time expressions.
Recognize and practice Past Simple irregular verb forms and question structures.

contextWarmup.prompt: Think about your best friend. What did you do together last weekend?
options: We went to the cinema and watched an action movie.
We stays at home and study math.
We is going to the park yesterday.
contextWarmup.explanation: Option A uses the correct Past Simple affirmative form went and watched with a past time context.

rules: Use Subject + Verb 2 for Past Simple affirmative statements, such as She went to Rome or They met yesterday.
Use Subject + didn't + Verb 1 for Past Simple negative statements, such as We didn't go to Rome or He didn't think.
Use Did + Subject + Verb 1 for Past Simple questions, such as Did you have a good weekend?
Use the double genitive structure, which is a or an plus noun plus of plus possessive pronoun or noun, to talk about relations, such as a friend of mine.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Using Verb 2 in Negative Sentences and Questions
commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use the past form, Verb 2, after didn't or Did, forgetting that the auxiliary verb already shows the past tense.
commonTrap.wrong: Did you went to the park yesterday? We didn't went home early.
commonTrap.correct: Did you go to the park yesterday? We didn't go home early.

content.contractionsTitle: Natural Spoken Contractions in the Past
content.contractionsSubtitle: Observe how auxiliary verbs and particles merge in everyday spoken English:

content.passageTitle: My Best Friend and Our School Trip
paragraphs: Last month, my best friend Leo and I went on a school trip to the science museum. We were very excited because we did not have any classes that day. Leo is a very cheerful person, and he always makes me laugh when I feel bored. On the bus, we sat together and talked about our favorite video games.

At the museum, we saw amazing dinosaur bones and old machines. Leo is very intelligent, so he explained many interesting facts to me. Later, we met a friend of mine from another school. We ate lunch together in the garden. It was a wonderful day, and we took many great photos.

Used when something is not necessary.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Describing Friends and Past Adventures

content.summary: Practical guide on writing about friendships, daily obligations, and past adventures using irregular verbs and double genitives in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Expressing Obligations
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + have to / has to + base verb
blueprintItems.example: I have to help my best friend on weekends.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Describing Past Actions
blueprintItems.example: We went to the museum last Saturday.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Using Double Genitives
blueprintItems.formula: Noun + of + possessive pronoun / possessive noun
blueprintItems.example: She is a close friend of mine.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'has to' for third-person singular subjects instead of 'have to'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: He have to finish his homework tonight.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: He has to finish his homework tonight.
mechanicsRules.why: Singular subjects like he, she, or a name require 'has to' for obligations.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always use the correct past simple irregular form in affirmative past sentences.
mechanicsRules.why: Past time expressions require the past simple verb form.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not add extra apostrophes when writing double genitives.
mechanicsRules.badExample: That is a friend of my sister's house.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: That is a friend of my sister.
mechanicsRules.why: The double genitive structure combines 'of' with a possessive form cleanly.

sampleSentences.en: I have to finish my homework before dinner.
We went to the cinema with our friends last night.
She is a wonderful friend of mine.
Did you see David at school yesterday?

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following affirmative sentence into a negative sentence using 'don't have to':
practicumQuestions.promptText: You have to clean your bedroom today.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'don't have to' before the base verb.
targetAnswers: You don't have to clean your bedroom today.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To express lack of obligation for 'you', use 'don't have to' followed by the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following sentence into the past simple tense using the correct irregular verb form of 'go':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Mark goes to the library with his friend.
practicumQuestions.hint: The past simple form of 'go' is 'went'.
targetAnswers: Mark went to the library with his friend.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The irregular verb 'go' changes to 'went' in the past simple tense.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct all capitalization and punctuation errors in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: on saturday, anna and me went to london.
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the day of the week, the proper name, the city, and use subject pronoun 'I' instead of object pronoun 'me'.
targetAnswers: On Saturday, Anna and I went to London.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Proper nouns and the beginning of sentences must be capitalized. Use 'Anna and I' as the subject.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform the following statement into a past simple question starting with 'Did':
practicumQuestions.promptText: You had a good time at the party.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'Did', change 'had' back to base verb 'have', and end with a question mark.
targetAnswers: Did you have a good time at the party?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Past simple questions begin with 'Did' followed by the subject and the base verb 'have'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using a double genitive structure ('a ... of mine'):
practicumQuestions.promptText: That is my friend over there.
targetAnswers: That is a friend of mine over there.
That is a friend of mine.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The double genitive combines 'a' or 'an' with a noun and 'of' plus a possessive pronoun such as 'mine'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with a correct past time expression meaning four days before today:
practicumQuestions.promptText: We met our old school friends _____.
targetAnswers: We met our old school friends four days ago.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Past time expressions like 'four days ago' specify when an action happened in the past.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence in the negative past simple form using 'didn't':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Tom bought a new jacket yesterday.
targetAnswers: Tom didn't buy a new jacket yesterday.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Negative past simple sentences use 'didn't' followed by the base verb 'buy'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using the third-person singular form of 'have to':
practicumQuestions.promptText: My sister have to finish her project tonight.
targetAnswers: My sister has to finish her project tonight.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Third-person singular subjects take 'has to' for obligations.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the spelling and punctuation mistakes in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: did you see david last night
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the proper name and add a question mark at the end.
targetAnswers: Did you see David last night?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Questions must begin with a capital letter, proper names require capitalization, and sentences must end with appropriate punctuation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence describing what you did last weekend using an irregular past verb:
practicumQuestions.promptText: What did you do last weekend?
practicumQuestions.hint: Example: I saw a movie with my friend.
targetAnswers: I saw a movie with my friend last weekend.
I went to the park with my friends last weekend.
I ate pizza with my best friend last weekend.
I met my best friend last weekend.
I bought a new book last weekend.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A complete sentence in the past simple uses an irregular past verb and a past time reference.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Friendship, Personality, and Daily Obligations

content.summary: In this speaking lab, you will practice talking about your best friends, describing their personalities, and explaining what you have to do every day. Focus on clear vowel sounds, correct syllable stress, and natural sentence rhythm.
content.audioGuidance: Listen carefully to the audio models. Notice how we stress content words like adjectives and main verbs while keeping helper words and modal expressions smooth and connected.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Pronounce vowels cleanly without stretching short vowels or clipping long vowels when speaking about feelings and daily habits.

pillars.name: Sentence Rhythm
pillars.explanation: Emphasize key words such as nouns, adjectives, and main verbs. Keep grammar words like to, do, and have unstressed in connected speech.

pillars.name: Modal Intonation
pillars.explanation: Use clear intonation when stating what you have to do or do not have to do in your daily routine.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the main stress stays on the first syllable cheer.
Notice how the stress shifts to the third syllable when we change to the noun form.
The stress moves to the final syllable in the noun form.
The stress shifts from the second syllable to the first syllable.

practicumQuestions.explanation: Speak warmly and use friendly intonation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Pronounce the sentence focusing on personality adjectives.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: My friend Nick is very intelligent and generous.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My friend Nick is very intelligent and generous.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ frend nɪk ɪz ˈveri ɪnˈtelɪdʒənt ənd ˈdʒenərəs/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Pronounce multisyllabic adjectives with correct stress peaks.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Pronounce the sentence using have to and don't have to.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: We have to wear uniforms, but we don't have to wear ties.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: We have to wear uniforms, but we don't have to wear ties.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wiː hæv tuː weə(r) ˈjuːnɪfɔːmz, bʌt wiː dəʊnt hæv tuː weə(r) taɪz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Contrast modal obligation clearly with accurate phrasing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice syllable stress in feeling adjectives.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: Are you feeling bored or excited about the party?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Are you feeling bored or excited about the party?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɑː(r) juː ˈfiːlɪŋ bɔːd ɔː(r) ɪkˈsaɪtɪd əˈbaʊt ðə ˈpɑːti/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Place stress correctly on the second syllable of excited.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Practice rising intonation for questions and falling intonation for statements.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: Do you like working together? Yes, I love teamwork.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Do you like working together? Yes, I love teamwork.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /duː juː laɪk ˈwɜːkɪŋ təˈɡeðə(r)? jes, aɪ lʌv ˈtiːmwɜːk/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use rising intonation on the question and falling intonation on the answer.
